text: Databases store and organize information so we can find it quickly. The most common type is SQL, which keeps data in tables with rows and columns. NoSQL databases are more flexible and often store data as documents, which suits changing information. To get data, we write queries, simple instructions that ask the database questions. Good data modeling means planning how tables connect before we start. Indexes also matter: they work like a book's index, helping the database find rows much faster. Choosing the right database and designing it well saves time and keeps data reliable.
